ORCL.summary: In this NYSE Live interview, Evan Goldberg, Co-Founder and Executive Vice President of Oracle NetSuite, discusses the introduction of NetSuite Quick Start and how artificial intelligence is helping reshape financial management for early-stage technology companies. Goldberg explains that while startup formation has accelerated in recent years, founders continue to face significant challenges when building the financial infrastructure needed to support long-term growth. Quick Start was created to help entrepreneurs establish a stronger operational and financial foundation from the beginning while minimizing complexity. A significant portion of the conversation focuses on AI-powered finance. Goldberg discusses how automation and intelligent financial tools can provide founders with improved visibility into key business metrics, including revenue trends, recurring revenue, cash management, profitability, and spending patterns. He explains how these insights can help startups make better-informed decisions as they grow. The interview also explores the relationship between Quick Start and the broader NetSuite platform. Goldberg describes how companies can begin with a streamlined financial solution and transition seamlessly to more sophisticated enterprise resource planning capabilities as operational requirements increase. This approach is designed to help organizations avoid disruptive financial system migrations during periods of growth. Another major theme is startup scalability. Goldberg discusses how milestones such as international expansion, multiple product offerings, and increasingly complex business operations typically drive the need for enhanced financial management systems. He explains why planning for growth early can help organizations remain agile and efficient as they expand. The conversation further examines lessons learned from supporting thousands of growing businesses. Goldberg highlights the importance of enabling founders to spend more time building products, serving customers, and driving growth rather than managing financial administration and back-office processes. Additionally, the interview discusses NetSuite's decision to offer Quick Start at no cost to qualified startups. Goldberg explains how reducing barriers to adoption can help entrepreneurs access financial tools and AI capabilities that may otherwise be difficult to implement at an early stage. Throughout the discussion, Goldberg provides perspectives on startup finance, artificial intelligence, financial automation, entrepreneurship, SaaS businesses, operational efficiency, business scalability, and technology-driven innovation.
